newsitem.title: USA: CPUC sets SoCal Gas performance-based rates.
newsitem.headline: CPUC sets SoCal Gas performance-based rates.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Wednesday approved a performance-based ratemaking scheme for Southern California Gas Co, the primary subsidiary of Pacific Enterprises.
Performance-based rate mechanisms, which replace traditional cost-of-service ratemaking, are structured to give utilities incentives to control costs.
The CPUC order, which is effective immediately, differs in several areas from the company's proposal.
The CPUC decision adopted a base margin of $1.315 billion, which reflects a decrease of just over $229 million.
SoCal Gas, however, said the new base represents a cut of around $160 million, since some public purpose programs and other costs are being reclassified.
The commission also acted to ensure that ratepayers receive the benefits of an expected decline in SoCal Gas' rate base.

Without such a rate design, SoCal Gas' entire revenue requirement would increase in future years, even though the portion of the requirement associated with rate base is lower, according to a statement from CPUC commissioner Henry Duque.

The new rate structure adopted a productivity factor that ramps up over time from 2.1 to 2.5 percent, which includes a one percent factor to account for the declining rate base, according to a commissioner advisor.

Duque also noted the SoCal Gas proposal did not include sharing of earnings, but the CPUC adopted a graduated sharing formula that allows shareholders to retain a larger percentage of earnings as SoCal's return exceeds the authorized rate of return.
The CPUC decision also grants the natural gas utilitygreater pricing flexibility.
The CPUC also said it denied SoCal Gas' request to offer new products and services, on an unregulated basis, through the tuiltiy or its affiliates.
The commission said it will take up the issue on a generic basis in a marketing affiliate rulemaking expected later this year.
